topic: Keeping up Pilates over the holidays: a 10-minute routine

slides.headline: Holidays? Keep 10 minutes for Pilates
slides.sub: A simple mat routine for a hotel room or a beach towel.

slides.title: Minutes 1 to 2: breathe and bridge
slides.body: Lie on your back, knees bent. Take five slow breaths into your ribs, then do ten bridges, rolling up and down one segment at a time. No rush, no gear needed.

slides.title: Minutes 3 to 4: dead bug
slides.body: Lie on your back with arms up and knees at 90 degrees. Slowly lower one arm and the opposite leg, then swap. Keep your lower back steady. Eight each side.

slides.title: Minutes 5 to 6: side-lying legs
slides.body: Lie on your side, hips stacked. Lift the top leg slowly, then do small circles. Ten lifts and five circles each way, then roll over and repeat on the other side.

slides.title: Minutes 7 to 8: bird dog
slides.body: On hands and knees, reach one arm forward and the opposite leg back. Pause, return and swap. Eight each side, moving slowly enough to keep your hips level.

slides.title: Minutes 9 to 10: open the spine
slides.body: Finish with cat-cow for ten slow rounds, then thread the needle for five each side. A good wind-down after a day of travel or a long lunch.

slides.headline: Pick up where you left off
slides.body: Our Pilates team can tweak your program for travel, then progress it when you're back. Book online via the link in bio.

caption:
Heading away for the holidays? Your Pilates doesn't have to go on hold. 🏖️

You don't need a reformer to keep your strength ticking over. Ten minutes on a towel is enough to hold onto most of what you've built.

The routine: breathing and bridges, dead bug, side-lying leg lifts, bird dog, then cat-cow and thread the needle to finish. Aim for three times a week. If anything feels sharp or wrong, skip it and keep the rest.

story.headline: 10 minutes of Pilates, anywhere
story.body: Bridges, dead bug, side-lying legs, bird dog, cat-cow. A towel is all you need. Three times a week.
